prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry of a laboratory aisle flanked by a fume hood and a multi-tiered lab bench, showing the camera wearer rotating left from the fume hood (frames 1–2) toward the adjacent bench and overhead shelves (frames 3–4) before turning right back toward the aisle and hood (frame 5). In frames 1, 2, and 5, a person seated on a chair (~1.5–2.5 m away) faces right into the fume hood and never looks toward the camera wearer, while the hood sash and near bench edges sit within the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.5–1.0 m) and the interior hood equipment sits within the seated person's reach (~0.4–0.7 m). Across frames 2–4, the two-tier shelving unit above the countertop and a nearby sink counter with a paper towel roll (~0.6–1.5 m away) move from the left periphery to directly in front of the camera wearer, with a vertical gas cylinder standing ~1.5 m beyond the sink (~2.5–3.0 m away) and the background corridor receding past 5–8 m. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradients clearly separate the overhanging upper shelves, foreground dispenser unit, and seated person's silhouette from the cluttered background benches and distant walls, as well as showing partial occlusions of the person's lower legs by the chair and bench edges at frame borders. However, the depth map is unreliable on the transparent glass sash of the fume hood—rendering it as a flat, bright opaque surface (~0.5–1.2 m) that masks the true recess of the interior workspace—and it blurs thin tubing and fine glassware on the shelves into merged depth blobs.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against the unlabelled laboratory background, identifying the seated person and their chair on the left in frame 1 (~1.5–2.0 m), shifting to the right in frame 2 (~1.8–2.2 m), disappearing out of view to the right in frames 3–4 as the camera turns left, and reappearing on the right in frame 5 (~2.0–2.5 m). In frame 1, two reagent bottles (~0.8–1.2 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach and ~1.0 m to the right of the seated person) are segmented inside the fume hood, while the chair partially occludes and borders the seated person's back and hips in frames 1, 2, and 5. As the camera pans across the opposite workbench in frames 3 and 4, only a single item on the middle shelf (~1.0–1.3 m away, within arm's reach of the camera wearer and ~0.3 m above the countertop) is segmented per frame, even though the person in frames 1, 2, and 5 consistently faces right with hands reaching into the hood ~0.5 m in front of their torso. This map makes it easy to track the exact pixel boundaries and relative screen positions of the person, chair, and selected containers without visual distraction from the dense lab clutter in the RGB image. However, it is highly unreliable for overall scene completeness and class accuracy: it misses almost all benches, shelves, and equipment, mislabels an upper-wall fixture as a 'tv' in frame 2, inconsistently labels the same green container on the shelf as a 'cup' in frame 3 and a 'bowl' in frame 4, and hallucinate a tiny 'person' mask on distant background equipment (~4 m away) in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body keypoints and skeletal links for the seated person in frames 1, 2, and 5, while remaining completely blank in frames 3 and 4 when the camera wearer turns left toward the shelving unit and the person exits the field of view. Across frames 1, 2, and 5, the yellow skeleton shows the person positioned on the left (frame 1, ~1.5–2.0 m), center-right (frame 2, ~1.8–2.2 m), and right (frame 5, ~2.0–2.5 m), consistently oriented in right profile with head keypoints facing right into the fume hood and never turning toward the camera wearer. The upper-limb keypoints show the shoulders, elbows, and wrists flexed forward and upward so the hands sit ~0.3–0.5 m in front of the torso inside the hood's workspace, well within the person's own reach but ~1.5–2.5 m from the camera wearer, with the hip-to-knee segments angled down and right on the chair seat. Compared to RGB, the skeletal wireframe strips away the loose white lab coat to reveal the exact joint angles of the spine, right shoulder, elbow, and hip, while reflecting how the lower legs are occluded below the knees by the fume hood base and lower frame edge. However, the map is unreliable for fine hand and full-body articulation: it fails to detect any magenta hand or finger skeletons in any frame, collapses the left and right body sides into an overlapping single-profile chain due to self-occlusion, and drops the lower-leg keypoints below the knee in frames 2 and 5.
